summary.text: St. Paulinus of Nola left a wealthy public career for an ascetic Christian life and became a bishop known for charity and poetry.
summary.reason: Concise, source-bound biographical teaching; source wording and later received traditions are distinguished from canonical Scripture.

saints.context: The source’s received ecclesiastical narrative is identified as such. Uncertain dates, later traditions and unknown circumstances of death are retained as uncertain.

blocks.text: The OCA describes St. Paulinus as a member of a wealthy family from Bordeaux who held high Roman public offices. Following conversion and baptism, he changed his way of life and distributed property to people in need. His wife shared this transition.
blocks.locator: Opening identification, public career and conversion

blocks.text: He pursued an ascetic life, received priestly ordination in Barcelona and later became bishop of Nola. The received life emphasizes his care for vulnerable people and captives. It also transmits a later story in which he offers himself in place of a widow’s enslaved son. That episode is presented as received hagiography, not used to reconstruct the military chronology of his lifetime.
blocks.locator: Ordination, episcopate and received ransom narrative

blocks.text: The OCA places his death on June 22, 431. This is distinct from the January 23 commemoration used in its calendar. Its account does not describe his death as martyrdom.

blocks.text: His surviving letters and poems preserve a Christian literary legacy. The life also remembers him as a builder of churches and a bishop whose generosity was central to his reputation.
